function: Transformer maps uplink beam-scan feedback maps to device distance and angle, then to codewords: two-stage coarse and fine near-field beam training for BS-direct or RIS-assisted beamfocusing (pp. 3-7).
system: Downlink near-field: ULA BS with N=256 antennas, passive reflecting UPA RIS with M=1024 elements, single-antenna device, carrier 60 GHz (pp. 3, 8).
method: Transformer with Conv1D embedding, attention modules and dense position detector; supervised on beam-scan maps and true positions, MSE loss, Adam, learning rate 0.001 halved every 50 epochs (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Own simulated near-field channel (4 paths, Gaussian gains), device angle U(-pi/3, pi/3), distance 3-100 m; 700 stage-1 and 7,000 stage-2 samples split 70/10/20 for training/validation/test (p. 8).
test_conditions: Same simulated distribution for training and testing (70/10/20 split), datasets per SNR from -10 to 20 dB; no unseen scenario, band or array size reported (pp. 8-9).
baselines: Learned only: CNN [23] near-field beam training and LSTM [39] beam selection, plus half-codebook variants; BS-direct versus RIS-assisted modes of the proposed scheme; no classical search method (pp. 9-11).
metrics: Beam selection accuracy, training and validation loss, normalized array gain, interference power, average achievable rate, versus SNR, distance and number of devices (pp. 8-11).
complexity: Analytical time complexity O(n^2 g) of the Transformer, FLOPs formulas per layer type and memory O(n^2 g) (pp. 7-8); no numeric FLOPs, runtime or parameter count reported.
q1_support: p. 8: "The channel gain for the LoS path is modeled" as k0 ~ CN(0,1), with NLoS gains CN(0,0.001). Own near-field simulator; no 3GPP TR 38.901, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 8: "validation, and 20% for testing." The test set is a held-out part of the same simulated data at the single setting of Table II; the SNR sweeps and the device positions of Figs. 8-10 do not count, and no other scenario, band, array size or dataset is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "CNN [23]: A DL-based near-field beam training scheme". The only baselines (Sec. IV-C, p. 10) are this CNN and an LSTM [39], both learned; no non-learned beam search (exhaustive, hierarchical or DFT codebook) is compared, and BS-direct versus RIS-assisted are two modes of the proposed scheme (Fig. 6, p. 9).
q4_support: p. 8: "resulting in a total time complexity" of O(n^2 g), with FLOPs formulas for convolutional, fully connected and attention layers (pp. 7-8); formulas only, no numeric values.
q5_support: p. 8: "scheme, we performed experimental simulations utilizing the" default configurations of Table II; data come from the authors' own channel generator (Algorithm 1, p. 6). No code or data link, DOI or public dataset appears in the paper.
notes: Area 3: beam training and selection is the learned function; the network predicts device distance and angle as an intermediate step and the reported metric is beam selection accuracy, so the localization exclusion was not applied, which the reviewer may confirm. q3 is 0 because the only baselines (CNN, LSTM) are learned and BS-direct is a mode of the proposed scheme, not a classical baseline. q4 rests on analytical formulas only.
